docs.description: I've been researching newly public domain films from 1929 and earlier, so I'm uploading the best possible copies that I can find. Regarded as one of the most influential films ever made, Metropolis was a financial disaster on release. It only made back about a fifth of its budget back. It didn't fare much better with critics or audiences at the time either. Since then it has become beloved by critics and film lovers worldwide, and is still considered one of the best science fiction pictures ever. The film follows a fiscally divided futuristic city that must unite if they are going to survive.

docs.description: Now Playing: 2 Silent classic Sci-fi films, "Metropolis" & "The Lost World" Phantom from Space (1927) NOT RATED - Directed by Fritz Lang, with Brigitte Helm, Alfred Abel, Gustav Fröhlich. In a futuristic city sharply divided between the working class and the city planners, the son of the city's mastermind falls in love with a working class prophet who predicts the coming of a savior to mediate their differences. The Lost World (1925) RATED PASSED - Directed by Harry O. Hoyt, with  Wallace Beery, Bessie Love, Lloyd Hughes. The first film adaptation of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's classic novel about a land where prehistoric creatures still roam.
